lesson.opening: What changes when a settlement becomes a city—and who organizes the work?

sections.heading: The institutional thread
sections.body:
Agricultural surplus and specialized work

Temples, kingship, taxation, and record keeping

The different geographies of the Nile and the Tigris–Euphrates

sections.heading: A model to test
sections.body: A connected account should move from food production and storage to coordinated labor, exchange, and record keeping. Do not make irrigation a single automatic cause of kingship. Distinguish physical remains from reconstructions of how institutions worked.

activities.prompt: “A surviving law collection tells us exactly how every court decided cases.” — is that an event claim or an interpretation?
activities.hint: A law collection is direct evidence for what its authors prescribed and claimed. Actual enforcement requires further evidence.
